question: The mean proportion of (3 + 2√2)2 and (3 - 2√2)2 is:
solution:
**Given:**

The numbers are (3 + 2√2)² and (3 - 2√2)².

**Formula Used:**

Mean proportion of a and b = √(a×b)

**Calculation:**

First, calculate (3 + 2√2)² and (3 - 2√2)².

⇒ (3 + 2√2)² = 9 + 12√2 + 8 = 17 + 12√2

⇒ (3 - 2√2)² = 9 - 12√2 + 8 = 17 - 12√2

Now, find the mean proportion.

⇒ Mean proportion = √[(17 + 12√2)×(17 - 12√2)]

⇒ Mean proportion = √[(17)² - (12√2)²]

⇒ Mean proportion = √[289 - 288]

⇒ Mean proportion = √1

⇒ Mean proportion = 1

**The mean proportion of (3 + 2√2)² and (3 - 2√2)² is 1.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Numbers = (3 + 2√2)² and (3 − 2√2)²

**Formula used:**

Mean proportion of a and b = √(a × b)

**Shortcut trick:**

Let a = (3 + 2√2)², b = (3 − 2√2)²

⇒ a × b = [(3 + 2√2)(3 − 2√2)]²

⇒ a × b = (9 − (2√2)²)²

⇒ a × b = (9 − 8)² = 1

Mean proportion = √(a × b) = √1 = 1

**∴ Mean proportion = 1**
